STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits on a white flat plate with a rim band and a flat centre, and there is no inner wall or bowl shadow. It is a square plate.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are usually 20-30 cm. This one looks medium-large, around 25 cm per side.
b) Reference: the salad and chicken sit on the plate. The cauliflower florets are about 4-5 cm across. Roughly 5-6 florets span the plate width, giving about 22-25 cm.
Reconciled width: 24 cm (square, area about 576 cm²).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Mixed salad greens (raw leafy, with carrot shreds and some dressing): covers about 25% of the plate, roughly 144 cm² at about 1.5 cm thick (mound averages half its peak). Volume about 216 ml; at 0.15 g/ml this is about 35 g. Adding dressing and carrot, estimate 50 g. Raw mixed greens about 20 kcal/100 g; dressing adds calories, so 35 kcal/100 g overall.
- Cauliflower florets (cooked/steamed): three to four clusters covering about 15% of the plate (about 86 cm²) at about 2 cm thick, mound about 1 cm average. Volume about 90 ml, density 0.6, so about 55 g. Steamed cauliflower about 25 kcal/100 g.
- Roast chicken pieces (skin-on, browned, the large piece plus smaller pieces): about 20% of the plate (about 115 cm²) at about 1.5 cm average thickness. Volume about 170 ml, density 1.0, so about 150 g. Roasted chicken with skin about 200 kcal/100 g.
- Shredded or braised meat/vegetable mixture (the darker, crumbly portion on the right, likely pork or chicken with onion and spices): about 12% of the plate (about 70 cm²) at about 1.2 cm average. Volume about 84 ml, so about 85 g. Estimate 170 kcal/100 g.

Hidden food: no clear base layer under the toppings. Plate is not heaped, so no extra base added.

STEP 4 - Total estimated weight is about 340 g, which is reasonable for a single plated meal of this kind.

STEP 5 - Energy:
- Salad: 50 g × 0.35 = about 18 kcal
- Cauliflower: 55 g × 0.25 = about 14 kcal
- Chicken: 150 g × 2.0 = about 300 kcal
- Shredded meat: 85 g × 1.7 = about 145 kcal
Total is about 480 kcal.
